Contracts.Title: Critique and redesign an original hypothetical school ramp model
SourceActivityComparisons: 1.1 Ratios Galore: corresponding right-triangle lengths and angles
1.2 Can You Calculate?: solve missing sides and explain underdetermination
1.3 Is it Accessible?: critique, model, draw and revise a ramp with guidance supplied by teacher; no original proprietary artwork reproduced
Contracts.OriginalPrompt: A school entry has four steps, each 7 inches tall. Sketch an original right-triangle ramp with a 28-inch rise. For a hypothetical design ratio rise:horizontal run of 1:12, label rise, run in inches and feet, sloped length, and the angle with the ground. Compare it with an independently chosen alternative ratio of 1:10: explain why these angles differ. Next analyze two same-angle ramps with rises 0.4 m and 1.0 m: give their run ratio and explain why neither absolute run is determined. Critique other real-world considerations (rails, landings, surface, width) without asserting any design is legally accessible. If the teacher provides verified current local accessibility specifications, assess compliance separately and redraw conditionally.

Criteria.Criterion: Correct 28-inch rise, unit conversion, horizontal and sloped lengths in two contrasting explicitly hypothetical designs
Clear original labelled ramp diagrams with right angles and consistent rise/run ratio
AA similarity proof for 0.4 m and 1.0 m with run ratio 2:5 plus two distinct valid absolute-run assignments
Critique/accessibility qualification and defensible revision with teacher-provided guideline provenance, not invented legal certification

IndependentEvidenceOracles.Expected: Rise=28 inches, run=336 inches=28 feet, hypotenuse=sqrt(28^2+336^2) inches

IndependentEvidenceOracles.Input: same steps, alternate hypothetical ratio rise:run=1:10
IndependentEvidenceOracles.Expected: Run=280 inches=23 ft 4 in; angle arctan(1/10), distinct from arctan(1/12)

IndependentEvidenceOracles.Input: same unknown slope angle with rises 0.4 m and 1.0 m
IndependentEvidenceOracles.Expected: run_1/run_2=2/5; runs 4.8 and 12 OR runs 4 and 10 both satisfy different common angles

NegativeAndEdgeReviewCases.Trigger: Treat 12 m as the unique second run without a known slope angle
NegativeAndEdgeReviewCases.ExpectedHandling: Require a ratio answer; explain missing-data ambiguity

NegativeAndEdgeReviewCases.Trigger: Unlabelled ramp sketch or missing units
NegativeAndEdgeReviewCases.ExpectedHandling: Teacher requests drawing and consistent units

NegativeAndEdgeReviewCases.Trigger: Zero run or non-positive rise when claiming a nondegenerate right triangle
Use foot units or a symbolic rise h with run=12h
NegativeAndEdgeReviewCases.ExpectedHandling: Accept if conversion and model assumptions are explicit

NegativeAndEdgeReviewCases.Trigger: Claim the classroom 1:12 model certifies current ADA legal compliance
NegativeAndEdgeReviewCases.ExpectedHandling: Reject legal certification; require verified local standard, full geometric and physical review

Contracts.Title: Equilateral altitude construction and five unknown 30-60-90 sides
SourceActivityComparisons: 3.1 Notice and Wonder: sketch vertex altitude
3.2 Decomposing Equilateral Triangles: measure halves and infer side ratio
3.3 Generalize Half Equilateral Triangles: five missing sides across three figures; optional after lesson 2
Contracts.OriginalPrompt: Construct and label equilateral ABC with positive side 2s, draw altitude AM from A to midpoint M of BC, and mark the right angle. Explain, using triangle congruence or symmetry and Pythagoras, why BM=MC=s and AM=s√3. Explain why 2s is the full side and not the short leg. Next solve five missing sides of three independently drawn 30°–60°–90° triangles: triangle I short leg 4 and hypotenuse 8, find long leg; triangle II short leg 6, find long leg and hypotenuse; triangle III long leg 5√3, find short leg and hypotenuse. State domain s>0 and justify why a degenerate zero or negative side is invalid, not merely numerically substituted.

Criteria.Criterion: Accurate labelled equilateral altitude, midpoint, 30°,60°,90° and full-side versus half-base distinction
Derivation AM²=(2s)²−s², AM=s√3 for s>0, not memorized ratio alone
Five exact missing side values 4√3,6√3,12,5,10 with correct opposite-angle mappings
Justified AA/generalisation across scale copies and clear degenerate/domain rejection

IndependentEvidenceOracles.Expected: short leg s, altitude s√3, hypotenuse 2s for s>0

NegativeAndEdgeReviewCases.Trigger: Use 2s instead of s for half-base or claim altitude=2s√3
Drawing omits perpendicular foot or labels
Use (√3/2) times full side instead of s√3
NegativeAndEdgeReviewCases.ExpectedHandling: Accept mathematically equivalent justified altitude expression
